name: Eventwright – Events Calendar & RSVP
author: matosius

sections.description:
Eventwright is a clean, fast events calendar for WordPress. It looks right in your theme, works in the block editor, and every feature in this plugin is free.

Moving from The Events Calendar? Eventwright imports your events, venues, organizers, categories, recurring series and RSVP guest lists in one click. Your old links keep working: /events/, /event/your-event/, /events/list/, /events/2026-12/, dated links of recurring events, the ?ical=1 feed people subscribed to, and even the [tribe_events] shortcode in your pages.

Calendar

  • Month view and week view. Both turn into an easy day-by-day list on phones.
  • List view with upcoming and past events, paging and category filter.
  • “Upcoming Events” block for home pages and sidebars (list or cards).
  • Works with block themes and classic themes. Styles follow your theme’s fonts and colors, or switch them off and style it yourself.
  • Fast: event dates live in their own indexed table, so big calendars stay quick.

Events

  • Start and end time, all-day and multi-day events, per-event timezone.
  • Recurring events: daily, weekly on chosen days, monthly on the same date or “the second Tuesday”, yearly. End never, on a date, or after a number of times. Add extra dates or skip dates.
  • Venues with address and map link, organizers with contact details.
  • Optional “Show map” button on event and venue pages (OpenStreetMap, off by default, loads only when clicked). A button in the venue editor finds the coordinates from the address.
  • Cost, event website, online event link.
  • Status: scheduled, cancelled, postponed or moved online (shown on the calendar and to search engines).
  • Event settings in the block editor sidebar. The classic editor is supported too.

RSVP

  • RSVP form on the event page, with places limit and “how many people”.
  • Confirmation email with an add-to-calendar link and a cancel link.
  • Email to you (or the organizer) for every new RSVP or cancellation.
  • Attendee list in the admin with filters and CSV export.
  • Waitlist: when an event or date is full, guests can join the waitlist. When someone cancels or you raise the limit, waitlisted guests are promoted in order and get an email with their cancel link.
  • For recurring events, guests choose a date and places are counted per date.
  • Spam protection without CAPTCHAs.

Import

  • One-click import from The Events Calendar (events, venues, organizers, categories, repeats, RSVPs).
  • Import from a calendar file or link (.ics): Google Calendar, Outlook, Apple Calendar or any iCalendar feed. Repeating events, all-day events and time zones are understood, a preview shows what will happen, importing the same file again updates events instead of duplicating them, and you can undo an import.

For developers

  • Documented actions and filters for add-ons: RSVP created, cancelled and promoted, attendee statuses, places per date, the RSVP form and its output, extra event detail rows and settings sections.

Calendar feeds and search engines

  • Subscribe links for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and Outlook.
  • “Add to calendar” links and a .ics file for every event.
  • schema.org Event markup on every event page, so search engines can show your dates, place and price.

Privacy

Eventwright does not track visitors and does not load outside scripts or fonts. It contacts an outside service only in the two cases described under External services below, and only after a person clicks a button. Map links open only when a visitor clicks them. RSVP data stays in your WordPress database and works with the WordPress personal data export and erase tools.

External services

Eventwright makes no outside requests on its own. Two optional features use outside services, and each runs only when someone clicks a button.

OpenStreetMap map (optional, off by default)

When you turn on Events → Settings → Show a map and a venue has latitude and longitude, event and venue pages show a Show map button. Nothing is loaded from OpenStreetMap until a visitor clicks it. After the click, the visitor’s browser loads the OpenStreetMap embedded map (https://www.openstreetmap.org/export/embed.html) inside the page. OpenStreetMap receives the visitor’s IP address and browser details, as with any web request, and the map area and marker position being shown.

  • Service: OpenStreetMap, run by the OpenStreetMap Foundation.
  • Terms of use: https://wiki.osmfoundation.org/wiki/Terms_of_Use
  • Privacy policy: https://wiki.osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Nominatim address lookup (admin only)

In the venue editor, the button Find coordinates from the address sends the address you typed (street, city, state, postal code and country) from your server to the Nominatim search service of OpenStreetMap (https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search) and fills in the latitude and longitude that come back. This happens only when a signed-in editor clicks that button. The request carries a User-Agent that names the plugin and your site address, as Nominatim’s usage policy requires. No visitor data is sent.

  • Service: Nominatim, run by the OpenStreetMap Foundation.
  • Usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/
  • Terms of use: https://wiki.osmfoundation.org/wiki/Terms_of_Use
  • Privacy policy: https://wiki.osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy

Calendar link import (admin only)

If you paste a calendar link in Events → Import, your server downloads that link once, when you click the button. The address is the one you typed; nothing else is sent. No service is contacted if you upload a file instead.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate Eventwright from Plugins → Add New.
  2. A page called Events with the calendar is created for you.
  3. Add events under Events → Add event.
  4. Coming from The Events Calendar? Go to Events → Import and click Import everything. Check a few events, then deactivate The Events Calendar.
sections.faq:
Will my old event links still work after switching from The Events Calendar?

Yes. The importer copies each event’s slug and your events and event address settings. When The Events Calendar is deactivated, Eventwright answers the same addresses, including list and month views, dated links of recurring events, the subscribe feed and the [tribe_events] shortcode.

Does the import change or delete anything in The Events Calendar?

No. The import only reads. You can run it again (it updates instead of making duplicates) or undo it.

What is imported?

Events (including drafts and private events), venues, organizers, categories and tags, featured images, recurring series, and RSVP attendees. Paid ticket orders are counted and listed in the report, but not imported yet.

Can I show the calendar on another page?

Add the Events Calendar block, or use the shortcode [eventwright_calendar]. Options: view="week" or view="list", category="music,talks", filters="no", per_page="20". For a short list use the Upcoming Events block or [eventwright_list limit="5"].

Can I change how the event page looks?

Add the Event Details and Event RSVP blocks to an event to place them yourself. Theme developers can copy templates/event-details.php or templates/rsvp-form.php into your-theme/eventwright/ and edit them.

Can I import from Google Calendar or Outlook?

Yes. Go to Events → Import, upload the .ics file you exported (or paste the public https link of the calendar) and check the preview. Repeating events are imported as repeats where possible; very special repeat rules are written out as a list of dates, and the report tells you which. Cancelled events are skipped. Importing the same calendar again updates the events you already imported. It is a one-time import, not a live subscription.

How does the waitlist work?

Turn on Waitlist when full for an event. When the event (or one date of a repeating event) is full, the form offers Join the waitlist. Guests are promoted in the order they signed up when someone cancels, when you trash or change an attendee, or when you raise the places limit. They get an email with their cancel link.

Does it sell paid tickets?

Not in this version. Paid tickets through your own Stripe account, with no extra fee per ticket, are planned.

Guests say they didn’t get the confirmation email

WordPress sends mail through your web host, and many hosts limit or filter it. Install an SMTP plugin so your site sends through a real mail service, and ask guests to check their spam folder.

I use a caching plugin. Will RSVP still work?

Yes. Eventwright works with page caching (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, host caches). The RSVP and cancel forms refresh their security token automatically when the page loads, so cached pages never show “The form expired”. No setup needed.

Does it work with my theme?

It was tested with Twenty Twenty-Five, Astra, Kadence, GeneratePress, OceanWP, Neve and Hello Elementor. Eventwright follows your theme’s fonts and colors. If something looks off in your theme, tell us in the support forum and we will fix it.

Is it translated?

All text is ready for translation through translate.wordpress.org.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: week view (switcher, block option, shortcode view="week", and /events/week/ links from The Events Calendar).
  • New: optional “Show map” button on event and venue pages (OpenStreetMap, off by default, loads only on click), and “Find coordinates from the address” in the venue editor.
  • New: RSVP waitlist with automatic promotion and an email to promoted guests. Waitlist status in the attendee list, filter and CSV export.
  • New: import from a calendar file or link (.ics), with preview, repeats, time zones, re-import without duplicates and undo.
  • New: hooks for add-ons (RSVP created, cancelled and promoted; attendee statuses; places per date; RSVP form and output; extra event detail rows; settings sections).
  • Added an External services section to this readme.

1.0.0

  • First release.
